About me

Words, body and movement, in one therapeutic relationship

I am an existential psychotherapist and a dance movement therapist. I have worked clinically since 2019 and have my private practice in Ilisia, at 111 Michalakopoulou Street; sessions are also available by video call.

I also work with the EPIPSY Day Hospital, the Melissa Network for migrant women and the Vima Koino health services centre.

I have worked with many different groups of people and have supervised front-line workers in the refugee field. I am a founding member of «Psychokinisi», a network of dance and movement psychotherapists.

I believe in growing all the time: since 2019 I have been in ongoing personal psychotherapy and supervision, I keep training in ways that enrich my work, and I present at international and European conferences.

Studies & experiencePsychokinisi network

The therapeutic approach

An integrative approach, with the body included

My approach is integrative, built on existential psychotherapy and dance movement therapy. At its heart is an equal, collaborative relationship, and the work is shaped with respect for each person’s unique way of being — exploring needs, meanings and wishes, as well as limits.

  1. Words
  2. The body
  3. Movement
  4. Meaning
  1. 01

    Words

    We talk about whatever is on your mind, with respect for your own way of being: your needs, your meanings, your wishes.

  2. 02

    The body

    We also pay attention to what the body says: bodily sensation, body image, psychosomatic difficulties.

  3. 03

    Movement

    Movement becomes a language too; what is hard to put into words can find expression through the body.

  4. 04

    Meaning

    Little by little the link between mind, body and emotion becomes clearer — and with it, your own way of being in the world.

Topics

What we can work on

Existential concerns

Lack of meaning, life transitions, existential anxieties and fears, coping with loss, and grief counselling.

LGBTQ+ affirmative therapy

Specialised support with questions of identity, gender and sexuality.

The body & psychosomatic difficulties

Exploring bodily sensation and body image and working with psychosomatic difficulties — the link between mind, body and emotion.

Emotional difficulties

Managing anxiety, mood swings, and improving the relationship with yourself and with others.

Questions

Before the first session

Where is the practice?

At 111 Michalakopoulou Street in Ilisia (115 27, Athens). The Ampelokipoi and Megaro Mousikis metro stations are about 650 and 700 metres away, with bus stops within 200 metres.

Do you offer online sessions?

Yes. Sessions are also available by video call, with the same 60-minute length.

How long is a session?

One hour (60 minutes), at the practice or by video call.

Do I need to know how to dance for dance movement therapy?

No. Movement is used as a way of expression and of getting in touch with the body, not as dance technique. We decide together how much, and when, movement becomes part of our work.

Can I talk about gender identity or sexuality?

Yes. I am trained in counselling and psychotherapy with LGBTQ+ people (Orlando LGBT+) and offer affirmative therapy on questions of identity, gender and sexuality.

Which languages do you work in?

I speak Greek, English and Spanish.

How do I pay?

By card or in cash. There is a reduced fee for people with disabilities, the unemployed and students.

How do I book?

By phone on +30 697 999 3808, by e-mail at marianna_ftk@hotmail.com, or online through doctoranytime.
